description: IRIS is a team of enthusiastic student innovators passionate about space exploration, healthcare technology, and artificial intelligence. We aim to develop an innovative software solution for monitoring astronaut health during space missions. We welcome creative thinkers, programmers, designers, researchers, and problem-solvers who are excited to collaborate, learn, and build technology that can make space exploration safer.
summary:
IRIS ASTRA is a web-based astronaut health monitoring prototype designed to support astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions. It brings physical health indicators, sleep patterns, physical activity, and psychological wellness together in a single interactive dashboard.

The system uses simulated health readings to demonstrate health monitoring and visualizes changes through interactive charts. It also includes a wellness questionnaire, configurable threshold-based early warning alerts, and health reports to help identify unusual readings that may require attention.

IRIS ASTRA addresses the challenge of astronaut health monitoring by demonstrating how multiple aspects of physical and psychological well-being can be tracked in one accessible platform. Its goal is to support early awareness of potential health concerns and contribute to safer, healthier, and more sustainable human space exploration.

The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Chart.js, and is hosted on GitHub Pages.
details:
IRIS ASTRA: AI-Powered Astronaut Health Monitoring and Early Warning System

IRIS ASTRA is a web-based astronaut health monitoring prototype designed to support the well-being and safety of astronauts during long-duration space missions. In space, astronauts experience challenging conditions such as microgravity, disrupted sleep cycles, physical stress, and psychological pressure. Monitoring these factors is essential for maintaining astronaut health and mission performance.

Our project provides a centralized dashboard to monitor and visualize important health indicators, including heart rate, body temperature, physical activity, sleep patterns, and psychological wellness.

How It Works:

IRIS ASTRA brings multiple health indicators together in a single interactive dashboard. It uses simulated astronaut health readings to demonstrate how health information can be monitored and analyzed. Interactive charts help visualize changes in health indicators over time.

The prototype includes:

  • Health Monitoring: Displays important health indicators such as heart rate and body temperature.
  • Sleep Tracking: Provides an overview of sleep patterns and rest duration.
  • Physical Activity Monitoring: Displays activity-related information.
  • Psychological Wellness: Includes a wellness questionnaire to help monitor emotional well-being.
  • Early Warning Alerts: Uses configurable threshold-based alerts to highlight readings that may require attention.
  • Health Reports: Provides summarized health information for easier review.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

IRIS ASTRA aims to demonstrate how a centralized digital health monitoring system could help identify unusual changes in astronaut health indicators at an early stage. By bringing physical health, sleep, activity, and psychological wellness information together, the system could support better health awareness and informed decision-making during space missions.

Its long-term vision is to contribute to safer and healthier human space exploration, particularly during extended missions where continuous access to medical professionals may be limited.

Tools and Technologies Used:

  • HTML for structuring the application.
  • CSS for designing a responsive and user-friendly interface.
  • JavaScript for application functionality and interactive features.
  • Chart.js for visualizing health data through charts.
  • Visual Studio Code for development.
  • Git and GitHub for version control and project hosting.
  • GitHub Pages for publicly deploying the website.

Creativity and Innovation:

The creative aspect of IRIS ASTRA is its integrated approach to astronaut well-being. Instead of focusing only on physical health measurements, it combines physical indicators, sleep, activity, and psychological wellness in one dashboard.

The threshold-based early warning feature demonstrates how unusual readings could be highlighted for attention. The interface is designed to make complex health information easier to understand through visualizations and clear alerts.

Factors Considered During Development:

Our team considered the unique challenges of space environments, the importance of monitoring both physical and psychological well-being, ease of use, clear visualization of health information, and the need for early identification of unusual readings.

The current version is a prototype using simulated data and illustrative alert thresholds. It is not a clinically validated medical device and does not provide medical diagnoses. Further development could include integration with wearable sensors, real astronaut health datasets, and more advanced analytical models.

IRIS ASTRA represents our vision of using technology to make future space missions safer, healthier, and more sustainable.
